minutes.headline: Capital Planning heard the school's FY24 capital requests; no votes taken, window film and a plow truck drew most pushback.
minutes.summary: The committee heard the superintendent and new facilities director present school capital requests for FY24, in priority order: window film, Turkey Hill doors, access control, fire alarm, athletic complex study and a pickup truck. Members debated the efficacy and cost of safety window film and questioned the truck's size and need, while supporting the door, access control and fire alarm items. Only a motion to adjourn was voted; prioritization is left for later meetings.

what_happened.line: The Capital Planning Committee took no votes on the school's FY24 capital requests; the only vote was to adjourn.
The school presented requests in priority order: window film, Turkey Hill doors, access control, fire alarm, an athletic complex study and a pickup truck.
Members debated the cost and effectiveness of the safety window film and questioned the size and need of the plow truck.
Members spoke more favorably of the door, access control and fire alarm items than of the film and the truck.
The next meeting adds minutes approval to its agenda, and members were asked to take notes for ranking the requests.

why_it_matters: These requests are the school's proposals for FY24 capital spending, which is mostly borrowed or taken from reserves and paid through taxes; the committee's ranking will shape which ones go forward.
Costs for the window film and the Turkey Hill doors rose between the school committee meeting and this one, so the amounts residents may be asked to approve at town meeting were still moving.
